**All ten pass the validator and all three `MapTargets` bands.** Three new themes — `tundra`, `ash`,
`marsh` — were added so every level gets its own palette; their tiles were generated automatically
from the ramp, since the tile script reads the registry.

## They are NOT balanced, and one is broken

Wave tables are copied from `crossroads` and not re-tuned. Routes differ, so the curve that lands
`crossroads` at 20.0% lands elsewhere here. Two sampled at 150 runs:

| Level | Runs lost | Lives | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `comb` | **42.0%** | 7.0, sd 5.9 | above the 15–30% band — hardest route in the set at 30 |
| `ringfort` | **0.0%** | 19.9, **sd 0.2** | unloseable |

**`ringfort` reproduces `gauntlet`'s failure exactly, and that is the interesting part.**

They are the only two maps in the repo built with **path-only corridors** — a forced route rather than
one the player shapes. Both come out unloseable with essentially zero variance (`gauntlet` sd 0.0,
`ringfort` sd 0.2), from completely independent layouts.

> **Two independent designs, same corridor technique, same degenerate outcome.** That is a second
> data point for the thesis in [gauntlet's cliff](reports/2026-08-07-gauntlet-cliff-balance.md): the
> problem is not tuning, it is that a forced route leaves the player no decision to get wrong. It
> also means `lane()` in the generator is a trap, and the other nine motifs deliberately use scenery
> instead.

`route-variance-metric` should be scheduled before any of these are tuned — tuning a map with zero
variance just moves where the flat line sits.

## How the generator satisfies bands that fight each other

`MapTargets` wants buildable at 35–55% **and** path 18–30, and the map report proposes density ≤ 2.0.
On a large grid those cannot all hold: at 20×9, 40% buildable is 72 cells against a route capped at
30, so density is 2.4 before anything else happens — and `crossroads` sits at 4.0.

Hence small grids (~13×12) with routes near the top of the band. Even then the last two bands pull
opposite ways, because a longer route needs more scenery and more scenery eats the buildable floor.
The generator's `thin()` runs two passes: the first keeps a block **only if it bends the route**,
buying length at the lowest cost in buildable; the second fills in anywhere, and neither may cross
37%.

Blind blocking was tried first and dropped six of ten maps to 26–34% buildable.

## Known Not Verified

- **No in-engine capture.** The display was down when these were generated, so the atlas is a
  top-down schematic rendered from JSON, not a screenshot. Each level still needs a look in the
  editor — `./run-editor.sh <id>` — before anyone trusts how it reads at the iso angle.
- Eight of the ten have not been balance-tested at all.
- `vs floor` is 1.0× on seven of them: the layouts do not force a detour, so the unmazed route is the
  Manhattan minimum. That matches `crossroads` and is not wrong — the player builds the maze — but
  `comb` at 2.1× is the only one whose geometry does real work.
